subject: gov.discourse
name: Media and platform monitoring after the events of 28-29 August 2026
milestone: Monitoring conclusions presented to media owners, 2 September 2026
position_end: The national communication observatory monitored traditional media, online media and the main publicly accessible digital platforms from 28 August to 1 September 2026 and presented its conclusions to public and private media owners in Niamey on 2 September 2026, at a meeting convened by the communications minister. It reported exceptional information intensity in the hours after shots and explosions were reported near an air base at the international airport and in sensitive districts of the capital, the effects of an information vacuum, divergence in how the facts were characterised, and social networks accelerating both information and disinformation, with old images and out-of-context video circulated. The observatory's president said the meeting was not a trial of the media nor a substitute for the authorities establishing the facts, and that an information vacuum does not suspend public demand for information but displaces it
note: the monitoring report itself is not published, so what was measured, over what sample and against what standard is not established; a state observatory monitoring platforms during a security incident is recorded here without a stated legal basis or retention rule
